hook_text: A bicycle is not one machine. It is four simple machines holding hands, and the trick is in the handshake.
clip_script: Turn an egg beater. Your hand goes in slow, the beaters come out fast. In between: gears. Input, process, output. Now a bicycle. Foot on pedal, that is a lever. Pedal on a crank. Chain to the back wheel. Wheel and axle on the road. Four mechanisms, and the output of each is the input of the next. Here is the handshake: mechanical advantage is load over effort, and in a chain the advantages multiply. A lever of two into pulleys of three is six. A car jack is a crank times a screw and a hand lifts a car. The catch: you pay in distance, every time. Your crane is crank, drum, pulley, magnet. The crank does the multiplying. The pulley just turns sideways into up. Read any machine with three questions: what goes in, what does each part do, what comes out.
visual_style: Whiteboard egg beater with arrows in and out; bicycle drawn as four boxes in a row; numbers two and three multiplying to six; crane chain of crank, drum, pulley, magnet.
mood: Curious and quick, taking machines apart with a grin.
pacing: Beater, bicycle, multiply, catch, crane, three questions, each a couple of seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace the chain in a machine at home.
